+# SWA ERP — Architecture Overview (for the server / app-dev team)
+
+*Forward this as-is. It answers the questions raised in the 24 Jun meeting: hosting, database, and what "the APIs" actually are.*
+
+---
+
+## 1. What this application is
+
+A single internal web application (ERP) for SWA. One backend, one database, one web frontend. Users reach it in a browser over the office VPN. No external/paid third-party APIs are involved.
+
+## 2. Deployment target (as discussed)
+
+- **On-prem Windows Server**, 128 GB RAM (extendable), currently used as file storage + RDP. IT confirmed it handles 100+ users.
+- Access: users connect over **VPN**, then open the app in a browser (a desktop shortcut to the internal URL, e.g. `http://swa-erp.local` or `http://<server-ip>`).
+- This app is light: a web server + an app server + one database. It will sit comfortably alongside the existing file-storage role.
+
+## 3. The three parts (all on the same server)
+
+```
+[ User's browser over VPN ]
+            │  HTTP (internal network only)
+            ▼
+[ Web frontend ]  React static files, served by the web server
+            │  REST calls on the same server  (these are the "APIs")
+            ▼
+[ App backend ]   Python (FastAPI) — business logic, auth, validation
+            │  SQL on localhost
+            ▼
+[ Database ]      ONE PostgreSQL instance — the single master database
+```
+
+## 4. Clearing up two points from the meeting
+
+- **"Are the APIs paid / external?"** — No. "API" here just means the internal REST endpoints our own frontend calls on our own backend, on the same server. Nothing leaves the network. No subscriptions.
+- **"Is there a master database, or separate databases?"** — There is **one master PostgreSQL database**. All modules (clients, inquiries, agreements, tokens, projects, documents, time logs, sustainability) are tables inside that one database, with proper foreign keys. We are *not* splitting data across multiple databases. (A single database is easier to back up, keeps relationships intact, and is the standard choice at this scale. If something needs isolation later, Postgres handles that with schemas — still one server.)
+
+## 5. Software to install on the Windows Server
+
+Two equivalent options — the server team picks based on their comfort:
+
+**Option A — Docker (recommended, simplest to operate)**
+- Install **Docker Desktop for Windows** (uses WSL2).
+- We ship a `docker-compose.yml`: it brings up backend + frontend + PostgreSQL + Redis in one command. Updates = pull new image, restart.
+
+**Option B — Native Windows services**
+- **PostgreSQL for Windows** (installer, runs as a Windows service).
+- **Python 3.11** + our backend, run as a service (e.g. via NSSM) behind **IIS** or **nginx** for Windows serving the React files.
+
+Either way: open one internal port (e.g. 80/443) on the LAN; no public internet exposure.
+
+## 6. Resource footprint (estimate)
+
+- Idle: ~1–2 GB RAM. Under 100 concurrent users: well under 8 GB. Negligible vs the 128 GB available.
+- Disk: the database is small (tens of MB of rows). Uploaded documents (DRN files) grow with usage — point them at the existing file-storage volume.
+
+## 7. Backups
+
+- One nightly `pg_dump` of the single database → onto the existing file-storage backup routine. That's the whole backup story. Document files back up with the file server as they already do.
+
+## 8. What we need from the server team
+
+1. Confirm OS (Windows Server — version?) and whether Docker Desktop/WSL2 is allowed.
+2. An internal hostname/IP + one LAN port for the app.
+3. A folder on the file-storage volume for uploaded documents.
+4. 15 min on a call to agree on Option A vs B.

+# SWA ERP — Scope & Data Model (v1, derived from source)
+
+**Source of truth:** the 20 Excel sheets in `resourses/ERP Sheets/` + the recorded meeting (24 Jun 2026).
+This document is what the client could not hand us as a written problem statement. We derived it ourselves from their data and their words. Every field below is copied from an actual sheet header — nothing invented.
+
+---
+
+## 1. The one rule that decides scope: interconnected vs independent
+
+The client was explicit: **build the interconnected chain first. Ignore the independent chains for the first build.**
+
+### IN SCOPE — the interconnected chain (first build, 8 modules)
+
+```
+INQUIRY ──converts?──► CLIENT (exists? reuse : create) ──► PROJECT
+                                                             │
+                  SERVICE AGREEMENT (yearly) ──► TOKEN ──────┤  (billing track, limited clients)
+                                                             │
+                              per project, per employee ─────┼──► DRN  (document referencing)
+                                                             ├──► TIME LOG
+                                                             │
+                              after project completes ───────┴──► SUSTAINABILITY METRICS
+```
+
+Note: **DRN and Time Log also occur OUTSIDE a project** (for Marketing and R&D work). Their link field is therefore polymorphic — it can point to a Project, a Token, or a Document. (See §3.7.)
+
+### OUT OF SCOPE for first build (defer or drop)
+
+| Item | Decision | Reason (from meeting) |
+|---|---|---|
+| **BOQ / Quotation (current Wave 3)** | **DROP from ERP** | Client: "we do not have any space for BOQ or quotation in ERP." This came from the rfq2boq product, which is **separate**. It was copied into our problem statement by mistake. |
+| Client Complaints | Defer | "we can also not have in the first build" |
+| Client Satisfaction / Feedback | Defer | same |
+| Marketing (Instagram / LinkedIn / Website) | Defer (independent) | independent chain |
+| R&D (Collaborations / Innovations) | Defer (independent) | independent chain |
+| HR independent sheets (Employees, Training, Hardware, Admin Process, Emp Feedback) | Defer (independent) | independent chain; keep models, no UI |
+
+**Result: first build = 8 modules.** Inquiries, Clients, Service Agreements, Tokens, Projects, DRN, Time Logging, Sustainability.
+Backend for all 8 already exists (wave-9). What's missing: frontend pages + Excel data migration + the last test fixes.
+
+---
+
+## 2. The business flow, exactly as the client described it
+
+1. An **Inquiry** enters the system first.
+2. If the inquiry **converts**:
+   - Check the **Client** database. If the client **exists** → go straight to **Project**. If it **does not exist** → create the **Client** first, then the **Project**.
+   - The inquiry becomes a project.
+3. For a **Project**, employees do **Document Referencing (DRN)** and **Time Logging**.
+   - DRN and Time Logging also happen **outside** a project (Marketing, R&D).
+4. After a **Project** completes → record **Sustainability Metrics** (the impact created).
+5. **Service Agreement + Token** track (parallel, for a limited set of clients):
+   - We sign a **Service Agreement for an entire year** — not project-by-project, a full-year engagement.
+   - A **Token** is the applicable billable unit under that agreement.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Data model — real fields from each sheet
+
+> ID convention seen in real data: `SWA-{YEAR}-{TYPE}-{NNN}`.
+> ⚠️ Discrepancy to confirm: Clients are `SWA-2025-CL-001` in the sheets (TYPE = **CL**), but our code uses **CLT**. Pick one. Recommend matching the sheets (**CL**) so migrated IDs are stable. DRN uses a continuous serial, not year-scoped.
+
+### 3.1 Inquiries — `Inquiries Sheet.xlsx` (37 real rows)
+`Sr No · Inquiry ID · Inquiry Date · Inquiry Type · Inquiry Source · Client Name · Requirement Summary · Estimated Value · Priority · Status · Owner · Technical Lead · Notes`
+- IDs: `SWA-2025-INQ-001…`  · Status: `Converted` / blank · Type: `Design` · Priority: `High`…
+
+### 3.2 Clients — `Clients Sheet.xlsx` (header row 2; data to be filled)
+`Sr No · Client ID · Client Name · Industry · Date Onboarded · Primary Contact · Email · Phone · Billing Address · Client Status · First Lead ID · First Inquiry ID · Notes`
+
+### 3.3 Service Agreements — `Service Agreements Sheet.xlsx` (real rows)
+`Sr No · Agreement ID · Client Name · Client ID · Inquiry ID · Service Name · Start Date · End Date · Total Tokens · Status · Notes`
+- e.g. `SWA-2025-SA-011 · ABCD · SWA-2025-CL-001 · SWA-2025-INQ-001 · INSUDESIGN · 2025-10-01 → 2026-03-31 · Active · Monthly Billing`
+- `Total Tokens` can be `N/A`. Status: `Active`.
+
+### 3.4 Tokens — `Tokens Sheet.xlsx` (**252 rows — the big migration**)
+`Sr No · Date · Token ID · Agreement ID · Token Type · Description · Token Status · Tokens Used · SWA Employee Name · Client Employee Name`
+- Token Status: `In Progress` / `Closed`.
+
+### 3.5 Project Tracking — `Project Tracking Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Project ID · Client ID · Inquiry ID · Client Name · Project Name · Start date · End date · Milestone · Progress Indicators · Status Updates · Team Leader · Project owner`
+
+### 3.6 DRN (Document Reference) — `Document Reference Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · DRN · Associated Project ID · Author · Document Type · Type · User · Description · Revision · Status · Remarks`
+- **DRN** = unique document number (primary key). Three-letter doc codes: **CON / DBR** (Design Basis Report), **GAD/GED** (General Assembly Drawing). Continuous serial.
+- `Associated Project ID` = FK to Project. `Type` = Submittal / Internal / Revision. `User` = Client / Reviewer / Authority (low value — candidate to drop, no downstream dependency). `Revision` = R0, R1… `Status` = approval state.
+
+### 3.7 Time Logging — `Time Logging Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · Employee Name · Employee Role · Work Type · Reference ID · Revision · Project Name · Activity Type · Software Used · Work Mode · Hours Logged · Billable Hours`
+- **`Reference ID` is polymorphic** — "primary linkage with project OR token OR doc."
+- **`Hours Logged` is in 0.5h intervals** (the sheet says so — *not* 15-min; update CLAUDE.md). `Work Mode` = Manual / Automatic. `Software Used` = dropdown (except Microsoft Office).
+
+### 3.8 Sustainability Metrics — `Sustainability Metrics Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · Reference ID · Compliant with Green Standards · Total Energy Saved (kWh) · CO2 emissions avoided (tCO2e) · Lifecycle Cost savings delivered (INR) · Insulation Efficiency (Actual/Expected) · Payback Period (Months)`
+- `Reference ID` links to a Project (`SWA-2025-PRJ-065`). Green standards: `No` / `GRIHA` / etc.
+
+---
+
+## 4. What's left to ship the first build
+
+| Layer | State | Owner |
+|---|---|---|
+| Backend models + API for 8 modules | ✅ exists (wave-9), ~23 tests red | running test-fix agents |
+| Frontend pages for 6 of 8 (Clients + Projects already exist) | ❌ 0 built | new OpenCode window(s) — see `work/wave-10/` |
+| Excel → DB migration (252 tokens etc.) | ❌ not written | new OpenCode window — see `work/wave-10/` |
+| Remove BOQ/Quotation from ERP nav/scope | ❌ still present (Wave 3) | follow-up |
+
+---
+
+## 5. Open items to raise with the client (specific, not "give me everything")
+
+1. **Client ID code:** sheets use `CL`, our code uses `CLT`. Confirm canonical → we standardize migration.
+2. **DRN `User` and `Document Type` columns** have no downstream dependency — keep or drop? (We recommend keep as free-text category, drop nothing destructive.)
+3. **Service Agreement `Total Tokens` = N/A** in some rows — unlimited, or unknown? Affects token-cap logic.
+4. **Time Log `Reference ID`** points to project/token/doc — confirm all three are real linkages we must support (we're building it polymorphic).
+5. Server-team call: confirm Windows Server, single PostgreSQL service, app reached over VPN via shortcut. (See `ARCHITECTURE_FOR_SERVER_TEAM.md`.)

+
+## The 20 sheets, grouped by build scope
+
+Scope decided in Meeting 2 (see transcript) and `../SCOPE_AND_DATA_MODEL.md`.
+
+### ✅ First build — interconnected chain (8)
+| Sheet file | Module | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Inquiries Sheet.xlsx` | Inquiries | 37 real rows |
+| `Clients Sheet.xlsx` | Clients | IDs use `CL` (code uses `CLT` — confirm) |
+| `Service Agreements Sheet.xlsx` | Service Agreements | yearly engagement; Agreement ID = source/channel |
+| `Tokens Sheet.xlsx` | Tokens | **252 rows** — main migration load; continuous numbering |
+| `Project Tracking Sheet.xlsx` | Projects | |
+| `Document Reference Sheet.xlsx` | DRN | continuous serial across doc codes (CON/DBR/GAD/KDR) |
+| `Time Logging Sheet.xlsx` | Time Logging | 0.5h intervals; Reference ID = project/token/doc |
+| `Sustainability Metrics Sheet.xlsx` | Sustainability | per completed project |
+
+### ⏸ Deferred — independent chains (build later if time permits)
+| Sheet file | Domain |
+|---|---|
+| `Instagram Metrics Sheet.xlsx` · `LinkedIn Metrics Sheet.xlsx` · `Website Metrics Sheet.xlsx` | Marketing |
+| `Research Collaborations Sheet.xlsx` · `Research Innovations Sheet.xlsx` | R&D |
+| `Employees Sheet.xlsx` · `Employee Satisfaction Sheet.xlsx` · `Training.xlsx` · `Hardware Issues sheet.xlsx` · `Admin Process Digitization Sheet.xlsx` | HR (restricted) |
+| `Client Feedback Sheet.xlsx` · `Client Complaints Sheet.xlsx` | CRM (explicitly out of first build) |
+
+### ❌ Not part of this ERP
+BOQ / Quotation — belongs to the separate **rfq2boq** product (confirmed Meeting 2).

+# Meeting 2 — Scope, Infrastructure & Decisions (24 Jun 2026)
+
+*Cleaned from the raw recording. Raw text preserved in `../_raw/meeting-transcript-original.txt`.*
+
+---
+
+## Infrastructure (client-stated)
+
+- **On-prem Windows Server** (99% sure it's Windows, client will confirm). Currently a **file-storage server** + some RDP usage. No other apps hosted.
+- **128 GB RAM** (extendable), good processor. IT says it handles **100+ users**. Compute is not a concern, but **optimize for efficiency**.
+- Access via **VPN**; users open the app via a **shortcut in their folders**. Most data entry happens on the server.
+- "Do we need SQL?" — client is **open to any configuration**.
+- Client will **connect us with the server-setup person** for a call to agree on architecture.
+- Client asked us to **share the architecture overview as text/screenshot** to forward to their app-dev team → delivered in `ARCHITECTURE_FOR_SERVER_TEAM.md`.
+
+## Architecture questions the client raised (and the answers)
+
+- "Are the APIs paid/external?" → No. Internal REST endpoints, same server, nothing leaves the network.
+- "Are you making a master database, or keeping it separate?" → **One master PostgreSQL** with FKs. (Client was wary of a single point of failure; addressed via backups + that one DB is the standard, relationship-preserving choice.)
+- Postgres currently runs on the dev laptop; free when self-hosted on their server.
+
+## Data & migration
+
+- Source of truth = **the 20 Excel files + this recording**. No separate written problem statement exists.
+- Data currently lives on **OneDrive**; everyone has access (no read-only yet — only ~3 months in).
+- **Migration ownership** is unresolved — "everyone has the data." → We own building the importer; they must validate output. (`scripts/migrate_excel.py`, see `work/wave-10/task-B-excel-migration.md`.)
+
+## Scope decisions (LOCKED)
+
+- **P0 / first build = 5 modules:** Clients, Inquiries, Service Agreements, Tokens, Projects.
+- **Plus the process modules:** Document Referencing (DRN) and Time Logging are part of the core process → include them. → **8 modules total** (add Sustainability, which closes a completed project).
+- **Interconnected vs independent:** *"Ignore the independent chains, focus on the interconnected chains."* Independent chains can come later if time permits.
+- **Defer / drop from first build:** Client Complaints, Client Satisfaction/Feedback, Marketing (IG/LinkedIn/Website), R&D (Collaborations/Innovations), HR independent sheets.
+- **BOQ / Quotation is NOT part of this ERP.** Client: *"we do not have any space for BOQ or quotation in ERP."* It came from the **separate rfq2boq product** and was copied into our problem statement by mistake. → Remove Wave 3 from ERP scope.
+
+## DRN sheet details (from the live screen-share)
+
+- Columns: Sr No · Date · DRN · Associated Project ID · Author · Document Type · Type · User · Description · Revision · Status · Remarks.
+- **DRN** = unique document number (**primary key**). 3-letter codes: CON/DBR (Design Basis Report), GAD/GED (General Assembly Drawing). Serial is **continuous**, code can vary.
+- `Associated Project ID` = FK from Project sheet.
+- `Document Type` (research/presentation/submittal) = **just categorization**, no downstream dependency.
+- `User` (Client/Reviewer/Authority) = **uncertain, maybe remove**, no dependency.
+- Note: the example sheet headers were **staggered by one column** — a minor data-entry offset to handle on import.
+
+## Process / communication notes
+
+- Client pushed back on being asked for "everything": *"it's not an MBA assignment… you have to use your brain and figure it out."* → We derive the spec ourselves from the sheets + recording (`SCOPE_AND_DATA_MODEL.md`), and only ask **specific, point-by-point questions** (a short list).
+- Client offered to connect us with **daily ERP users** (e.g. marketing team) for module-specific walkthroughs.
+- They want: the **architecture text**, a **live demo**, and our **specific question list**.
+
+## Our follow-up question list (specific, not open-ended)
+
+1. Client ID code: sheets use `CL`, our code uses `CLT` — which is canonical?
+2. DRN `User` / `Document Type` columns — keep as free-text category or drop?
+3. Service Agreement `Total Tokens = N/A` — unlimited or unknown?
+4. Confirm Time Log `Reference ID` must support project + token + document linkages.
+5. Confirm Windows Server version + whether Docker/WSL2 is allowed (for the server-team call).

+# Meeting 1 — Business Flow Walkthrough (SWA team)
+
+*Cleaned from the raw recording. Speakers: SWA team (Viraj's team — Balram + a software engineer). Raw text preserved in `../_raw/meeting-transcript-original.txt`.*
+
+---
+
+## The core flow (their words, organized)
+
+1. **Inquiry comes in** → if it converts, it becomes a **Client** (client name + generated Client ID).
+2. Based on the client's requirement, they generate **documents** for the work.
+3. **Service Agreements:** they currently have ~3–4 active agreements. An agreement ID is tied to **where the work comes from** (the channel/source), not to a single project.
+4. **Tokens:** when work (e.g. an IEP/SPL job) comes through an agreement, they create a **Token** under that Agreement ID.
+5. **DRN (Document Reference Number):** generated for each document produced. The DRN ID is also written back onto the token/document, so each ID has a defined flow.
+6. If the client needs energy-efficiency / requirement documents, they fill the relevant sheets.
+
+## Primary key / foreign key structure
+
+- Sheets are linked by **primary key / foreign key**. The segmentation/agreement sheet links to the **Token** sheet, which links to the **DRN** sheet, then **Time Logging**.
+- Some sheets are **independent** (open to everyone); some are restricted (HR: admin, employee satisfaction; Finance: founder-only).
+
+## How they actually work day-to-day (the 4 main sheets)
+
+> "Mainly we are writing with only four sheets" — Agreement/Segmentation, Token, DRN, Time Logging.
+
+1. **Identify the source** of a new lead (e.g. IESK, APEX consulting, an MEP consultant, a PTM industry contact). Each source has its own **Agreement ID**.
+2. Copy that **Agreement ID** → go to the **Token** sheet → create the token. **Token numbers are continuous across years** (e.g. 1801 last year, 2021 this year → next is 188, etc.).
+3. After the token, generate a new **DRN / DBR ID** in the Document Reference sheet. Inputs: doc type code (e.g. DBR = Design Basis Report) + the DRN ID. **The DRN serial is continuous regardless of the 3-letter code** — "after 138 it is 139; if it's KDR it's still 139."
+4. When the work is done, the DRN number is written into the delivered document (Word) and sent to the client.
+5. **Time Logging:** the employee logs against a **Reference ID** (token/project/doc), with description, the website/asset created, and **available hours** (e.g. "this took 2–3 hours") — they record estimated billable time in those buckets.
+
+## Independent / R&D flow (parallel, same shape)
+
+- For **independent / Reforge (R&D) tasks**: Reforge generation → DRN sheet → Time Logging.
+- Example: a research topic ("guidebook for thermal") gets an ID like `INN-074`; copy that into the DRN sheet, generate the document, then log time against it.
+- "Most of our projects are from certification."
+
+## Sustainability metrics
+
+- Recorded per project: **carbon savings, energy savings, insulation efficiency, payback period, lifecycle cost**.
+- Plan: in future, add a sustainability entry when the client's ID is figured out.
+
+## What the team said about deliverables / ownership
+
+- "We are doing this flow **live** currently, but the **final flow is decided by Viraj**." Data entries and final settings will come from Viraj.
+- They acknowledged we (the dev side) need **clear written notes / a problem statement** — but see Meeting 2 for how that conversation went.
+
+## Key facts to bake into the system
+
+- **Agreement ID = source/channel identifier** (one agreement spans many projects/tokens for that source).
+- **Token numbers: continuous, year-agnostic** running serial.
+- **DRN serial: continuous across all doc-type codes** (CON/DBR/KDR/GAD share one running number).
+- **Time logging Reference ID is polymorphic** (project / token / document).
+- Restricted sheets exist (HR → HR only; Finance → founder only) → RBAC must reflect this.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Excel -> DB migration for the SWA ERP first build (8 interconnected modules).
+
+Reads resourses/ERP Sheets/*.xlsx and loads Inquiries, Clients, Service
+Agreements, Tokens, Projects, DRN, Time Logging and Sustainability into the
+database in dependency order. Idempotent: rows whose business id already exists
+are skipped. Required parent rows that are referenced but missing (e.g. an
+agreement referenced by a token) are created as stubs and reported.
+
+Usage:
+    python scripts/migrate_excel.py --dry-run
+    python scripts/migrate_excel.py --commit
+    python scripts/migrate_excel.py --commit --only tokens
+
+DB target: env DATABASE_URL, else the app default (postgresql://swa:swa@localhost:5432/swa_erp).
+Never writes to the Excel files.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+import uuid
+from datetime import date, datetime
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import openpyxl
+from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker
+
+# Make src importable
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+
+from src.backend.core.security import hash_password  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.db.base import Base  # noqa: E402
+import src.backend.models  # noqa: F401,E402  (register all models)
+from src.backend.models.client import Client  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.drn import DRN  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.inquiry import Inquiry  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.project import Project  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.service_agreement import ServiceAgreement  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.sustainability import SustainabilityMetric  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.time_log import TimeLog  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.token import Token  # noqa: E402
+from src.backend.models.user import User  # noqa: E402
+
+SHEETS_DIR = ROOT / "resourses" / "ERP Sheets"
+DB_URL = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://swa:swa@localhost:5432/swa_erp")
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- coercion ----
+
+def norm(s: object) -> str:
+    """Normalize a header cell for fuzzy matching."""
+    return "".join(ch for ch in str(s or "").lower() if ch.isalnum())
+
+
+def clean(v: object) -> str | None:
+    if v is None:
+        return None
+    s = str(v).strip()
+    if s == "" or s.upper() in {"N/A", "NA", "-", "NULL", "NONE"}:
+        return None
+    return s
+
+
+def to_date(v: object) -> date | None:
+    if v is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(v, datetime):
+        return v.date()
+    if isinstance(v, date):
+        return v
+    s = clean(v)
+    if not s:
+        return None
+    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d", "%d-%m-%Y", "%d/%m/%Y", "%m/%d/%Y", "%Y/%m/%d"):
+        try:
+            return datetime.strptime(s[:10], fmt).date()
+        except ValueError:
+            continue
+    return None
+
+
+def to_decimal(v: object) -> Decimal | None:
+    s = clean(v)
+    if not s:
+        return None
+    s = s.replace(",", "").replace("₹", "").replace("INR", "").strip()
+    try:
+        return Decimal(s)
+    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
+        return None
+
+
+def to_int(v: object) -> int | None:
+    d = to_decimal(v)
+    return int(d) if d is not None else None
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------- sheet reader ----
+
+def load_rows(filename: str, anchor_headers: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
+    """Return a list of {normalized_header: value} dicts.
+
+    Auto-detects the header row by finding the first row that contains all the
+    given anchor header labels (normalized). Skips a possible annotation row
+    directly under the header (a row whose first cell is a meaning/why label).
+    """
+    path = SHEETS_DIR / filename
+    if not path.exists():
+        return []
+    # Not read_only: read_only mode truncates iter_rows when the stored sheet
+    # dimension is wrong (these sheets under-report their row count).
+    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
+    ws = wb.worksheets[0]
+    rows = [list(r) for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]
+    wb.close()
+    if not rows:
+        return []
+
+    anchors = {norm(a) for a in anchor_headers}
+    header_idx = None
+    for i, r in enumerate(rows[:6]):
+        cells = {norm(c) for c in r if c is not None}
+        if anchors.issubset(cells):
+            header_idx = i
+            break
+    if header_idx is None:
+        return []
+
+    header = [norm(c) for c in rows[header_idx]]
+    out: list[dict] = []
+    for r in rows[header_idx + 1:]:
+        # skip annotation rows ("meaning", "why it exists", "column name")
+        first = norm(r[0]) if r else ""
+        if first in {"meaning", "whyitexists", "columnname", "column"}:
+            continue
+        rec = {}
+        nonempty = False
+        for h, val in zip(header, r):
+            if not h:
+                continue
+            rec[h] = val
+            if clean(val) is not None:
+                nonempty = True
+        if nonempty:
+            out.append(rec)
+    return out
+
+
+def get(rec: dict, *aliases: str) -> object:
+    for a in aliases:
+        k = norm(a)
+        if k in rec:
+            return rec[k]
+    return None
+
+
+# Values that mean "this row is a repeated header / annotation", not real data
+HEADER_ECHO = {
+    "tokenid", "agreementid", "clientid", "projectid", "inquiryid",
+    "drn", "referenceid", "srno", "srno.", "columns", "column", "columnname",
+}
+
+
+def is_echo(biz: object) -> bool:
+    """True for repeated-header / legend / example template rows.
+
+    The source sheets carry annotation rows ("Primary Key", "Doc Ref No",
+    "Unique document number", "Design Basis Report"...). Real business IDs are
+    SWA-codes or bare numbers and never contain spaces, so a multi-word value
+    that is not an SWA code is a template row, not data.
+    """
+    if norm(biz) in HEADER_ECHO:
+        return True
+    s = str(biz or "").strip()
+    return " " in s and not s.lower().startswith("swa")
+
+
+def cap(s: str | None, n: int) -> str | None:
+    """Clamp a string to a column's max length (defensive against junk cells)."""
+    if s is None:
+        return None
+    return s[:n]
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ----
+
+class Report:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.lines: list[str] = []
+        self.counts: dict[str, dict] = {}
+
+    def module(self, name: str, parsed: int, inserted: int, skipped: int, stubs: int = 0, notes: str = "") -> None:
+        self.counts[name] = dict(parsed=parsed, inserted=inserted, skipped=skipped, stubs=stubs, notes=notes)
+
+    def render(self) -> str:
+        w = max([len(k) for k in self.counts] + [8])
+        head = f"{'module'.ljust(w)}  parsed  insert   skip   stub  notes"
+        out = [head, "-" * len(head)]
+        for k, v in self.counts.items():
+            out.append(f"{k.ljust(w)}  {v['parsed']:>6}  {v['inserted']:>6}  {v['skipped']:>5}  {v['stubs']:>5}  {v['notes']}")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers ----
+
+PLACEHOLDER_PW = None  # lazy
+
+
+def _pw() -> str:
+    global PLACEHOLDER_PW
+    if PLACEHOLDER_PW is None:
+        PLACEHOLDER_PW = hash_password(uuid.uuid4().hex)
+    return PLACEHOLDER_PW
+
+
+_UNKNOWN_CLIENT_ID: uuid.UUID | None = None
+
+
+def unknown_client(db: Session) -> uuid.UUID:
+    """Singleton fallback client for rows whose client cannot be resolved
+    (service_agreements.client_id and projects.client_id are NOT NULL)."""
+    global _UNKNOWN_CLIENT_ID
+    if _UNKNOWN_CLIENT_ID is not None:
+        return _UNKNOWN_CLIENT_ID
+    c = db.execute(select(Client).where(Client.code == "IMPORT-UNKNOWN")).scalars().first()
+    if not c:
+        c = Client(
+            name="(Unknown — imported)",
+            code="IMPORT-UNKNOWN",
+            primary_email="unknown@import.swa.local",
+            client_status="Active",
+        )
+        db.add(c)
+        db.flush()
+    _UNKNOWN_CLIENT_ID = c.id
+    return c.id
+
+
+def get_or_create_user(db: Session, name: str | None, cache: dict, stubs: list) -> uuid.UUID | None:
+    name = clean(name)
+    if not name:
+        return None
+    key = name.lower()
+    if key in cache:
+        return cache[key]
+    u = db.execute(select(User).where(User.name == name)).scalars().first()
+    if not u:
+        u = User(
+            email=f"{norm(name) or uuid.uuid4().hex}@import.swa.local",
+            name=name,
+            password_hash=_pw(),
+            role="viewer",
+            is_active=False,
+        )
+        db.add(u)
+        db.flush()
+        stubs.append(name)
+    cache[key] = u.id
+    return u.id
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------- per-module -----
+
+def mig_inquiries(db: Session, rep: Report) -> None:
+    rows = load_rows("Inquiries Sheet.xlsx", ["Inquiry ID"])
+    ins = skip = 0
+    for r in rows:
+        biz = clean(get(r, "Inquiry ID"))
+        if not biz or is_echo(biz):
+            continue
+        if db.execute(select(Inquiry).where(Inquiry.inquiry_id == biz)).scalars().first():
+            skip += 1
+            continue
+        owner = clean(get(r, "Owner"))
+        lead = clean(get(r, "Technical Lead"))
+        extra = " ".join(x for x in [f"Owner: {owner}" if owner else "", f"Tech Lead: {lead}" if lead else ""] if x)
+        notes = clean(get(r, "Notes")) or ""
+        db.add(Inquiry(
+            inquiry_id=biz,
+            inquiry_date=to_date(get(r, "Inquiry Date")) or date.today(),
+            inquiry_type=cap(clean(get(r, "Inquiry Type")), 32) or "Other",
+            inquiry_source=clean(get(r, "Inquiry Source")),
+            client_name=clean(get(r, "Client Name")) or "Unknown",
+            requirement_summary=clean(get(r, "Requirement Summary")),
+            estimated_value=to_decimal(get(r, "Estimated Value")),

+    g.add_argument("--commit", action="store_true", help="insert into the database")
+    ap.add_argument("--only", choices=list(MODULES), help="run a single module")

+
+    if not SHEETS_DIR.exists():
+        print(f"ERROR: sheets dir not found: {SHEETS_DIR}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    engine = create_engine(DB_URL, future=True)
+    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine, checkfirst=True)
+    SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False, autocommit=False, expire_on_commit=False)
+
+    order = [args.only] if args.only else ORDER
+    rep = Report()
+    db = SessionLocal()
+    try:
+        for name in order:
+            MODULES[name](db, rep)
+            db.flush()
+        if args.commit:
+            db.commit()
+        else:
+            db.rollback()
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

+    finally:

+    print(f"DB: {DB_URL}\n")
+    print(rep.render())
+    return 0

 """Business-ID generator.
 
 Produces IDs like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`. Uses a DB-backed sequence counter
 (`IdSequence`) so each (type_code, year) pair advances atomically.
 
 Pass `year=0` for "continuous across years" (per meeting: DBR/CAS/GAD numbers
 do not reset per year).
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from datetime import datetime
 
 from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
 
 from src.backend.models.id_sequence import IdSequence
 
 
 def current_year() -> int:
     return datetime.utcnow().year
 
 
 def next_business_id(db: Session, type_code: str, year: int | None = None) -> str:
     """Generate the next business ID for `type_code`.
 
     Args:
         db: SQLAlchemy session.
         type_code: Short code like `CLT`, `INQ`, `SA`, `TKN`, `PRJ`, `EMP`,
             `FDB`, `TRN`, `HW`, `PROC`, `COL`, `INN`, `FB`, `CMP`,
             `IG`, `LI`, `WEB`, `CON`, `DBR`, `CAS`, `GAD`, `KDR`, `RDP`,
             `VAL`, `RPT`, `OTH`.
         year: Calendar year (defaults to current year). Pass `0` for
             continuous counters (e.g. DBR numbers per the meeting transcript).
 
     Returns:
         A formatted ID string like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`.
     """
     if year is None:
         year = current_year()
 
     seq = (
         db.query(IdSequence)
         .filter_by(type_code=type_code, year=year)
         .with_for_update()
         .one_or_none()
     )
     if seq is None:
         seq = IdSequence(type_code=type_code, year=year, last_value=0)
         db.add(seq)
         db.flush()
 
     seq.last_value += 1
     db.flush()

 ) -> tuple[list[Token], int]:

 def update_token(
     db: Session,
     token_id: uuid.UUID,
     update_data: dict,
     updated_by: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
 ) -> Token | None:
     token = get_token(db, token_id)
     if not token:
         return None
 
     old_status = token.token_status
     for key, value in update_data.items():
         if hasattr(token, key) and value is not None:
             setattr(token, key, value)
 
     db.commit()
     db.refresh(token)
 
     if old_status != token.token_status:
         create_entry(
             db,
             action="token.status_transition",
             entity_type="token",
             entity_id=token.id,
             user_id=updated_by,
             after_json={
                 "token_id": token.token_id,
                 "from_status": old_status,
                 "to_status": token.token_status,
             },
         )
 
     return token
 
 
 def delete_token(
     db: Session,
     token_id: uuid.UUID,
     deleted_by: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
 ) -> bool:
     token = get_token(db, token_id)
     if not token:
         return False
 
     token_status = token.token_status
     if token_status not in {TokenStatus.CANCELLED, TokenStatus.CLOSED}:
         raise TokenServiceError(
             f"Cannot delete token with status '{token_status}'. "
             "Only 'Cancelled' or 'Closed' tokens can be deleted."
         )
 
     db.delete(token)
     db.commit()
 
     create_entry(
         db,
         action="token.delete",
         entity_type="token",
         entity_id=token_id,
         user_id=deleted_by,
         after_json={
             "token_id": token.token_id,
             "token_status": token_status,
         },
     )
 
     return True
 
 
 def transition_token_status(
     db: Session,
     token_id: uuid.UUID,
     new_status: str,
     transitioned_by: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
 ) -> Token | None:
     token = get_token(db, token_id)
     if not token:
         return None
 
     if not can_transition_status(token.token_status, new_status):
         raise TokenServiceError(
             f"Invalid status transition from '{token.token_status}' to '{new_status}'"
         )
 
     old_status = token.token_status
     token.token_status = new_status
 
     if new_status == TokenStatus.CLOSED and token.tokens_used:
         agreement = (
             db.query(ServiceAgreement)
             .filter(ServiceAgreement.id == token.agreement_id)
             .first()
         )
         if agreement:
             agreement.total_tokens = (
                 (agreement.total_tokens or 0) + float(token.tokens_used)
             )
             db.commit()
 
     db.commit()
     db.refresh(token)
 
     create_entry(
         db,
         action="token.status_transition",
         entity_type="token",
         entity_id=token.id,
         user_id=transitioned_by,
         after_json={
             "token_id": token.token_id,
             "from_status": old_status,
             "to_status": new_status,
             "tokens_used": float(token.tokens_used) if token.tokens_used else None,
         },
     )
 
     return token
 
 
 def get_tokens_by_agreement(db: Session, agreement_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Token]:
     return db.query(Token).filter(Token.agreement_id == agreement_id).all()

+import bcrypt as _bcrypt
+_original_gensalt = _bcrypt.gensalt

+# Wave 10 — First Build Completion (P0 interconnected chain)
+
+Scope locked in `SCOPE_AND_DATA_MODEL.md`. Backend for the 8 in-scope modules already exists.
+This wave finishes the **frontend pages** and the **Excel → DB migration** so the first build is demoable on real data.
+
+## In-scope modules (8)
+Inquiries · Clients · Service Agreements · Tokens · Projects · DRN · Time Logging · Sustainability.
+(Clients + Projects pages already exist — reuse their patterns.)
+
+## File-ownership map (prevents the parallel-agent conflicts from wave-9)
+| Window | Task file | Owns these paths exclusively | Model |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Test-fix agents (already running) | `work/wave-9/fixes/*` | `src/backend/**`, `tests/**` | (running) |
+| **NEW Window 1** | `task-A-frontend-pages.md` | `src/frontend/**` only | strong coder (Sonnet/GPT-class) |
+| **NEW Window 2** | `task-B-excel-migration.md` | `scripts/migrate_excel.py` only | strong coder |
+
+Frontend and migration do not touch backend source, so they won't collide with the test-fix agents.
+Within frontend, **one** window owns all of `src/frontend` to avoid shared-file (App.tsx, api.ts, types, Sidebar) merge conflicts. Do **not** split frontend across two windows until the shared scaffolding from Task A has landed.
+
+## How to dispatch each new window
+1. Open a new OpenCode window in this repo.
+2. Paste `work/WORKER_PROMPT.md`.
+3. Paste the one task file for that window.
+4. Worker writes code + a report to `work/reports/wave-10/`.
+
+## Acceptance (orchestrator runs before merge)
+- Frontend: `cd src/frontend && npm run build` passes; all 8 modules appear in the sidebar; each list page loads against the live backend (`make dev`).
+- Migration: `python scripts/migrate_excel.py --dry-run` prints row counts per sheet with zero errors; `--commit` loads them; `scripts/demo_live_api.py` then lists real rows.

"""Base CRUD service helper for HR bundle modules.

Provides common CRUD operations for HR-related entities.
"""

import uuid
from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

T = TypeVar("T")


def list_items(db: Session, page: int, page_size: int, q: str | None = None) -> tuple[list, int]:
    """Default list implementation - can be overridden by service."""
    return [], 0


def get_by_id(db: Session, item_id: uuid.UUID):
    """Default get_by_id - override in service."""
    return None


def create(db: Session, **kwargs):
    """Default create - override in service."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def update(db: Session, item) -> object:
    """Default update - override in service."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def soft_delete(db: Session, item) -> object:
    """Default soft_delete - override in service."""
    raise NotImplementedError


class BaseCRUDService(Generic[T]):
    """Base CRUD service for HR entities."""

    def __init__(self, model, repo_module=None):
        self.model = model
        self.repo = repo_module

    def list_items(
        self,
        db: Session,
        page: int = 1,
        page_size: int = 20,
        q: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[list[T], int, int, int]:
        """List items with pagination and search."""
        query = db.query(self.model).filter(self.model.deleted_at.is_(None))
        if q and hasattr(self.model, "name"):
            query = query.filter(self.model.name.ilike(f"%{q}%"))
        total = query.count()
        offset = (page - 1) * page_size
        items = query.order_by(self.model.created_at.desc()).offset(offset).limit(page_size).all()
        return list(items), total, page, page_size

    def get_item(self, db: Session, item_id: uuid.UUID) -> T | None:
        """Get item by ID."""
        return db.query(self.model).filter(self.model.id == item_id, self.model.deleted_at.is_(None)).first()

    def create_item(
        self,
        db: Session,
        data: Any,
        actor_id: uuid.UUID | None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> T:
        """Create item."""
        from datetime import datetime
        from src.backend.core.id_gen import next_business_id

        # Get type code from model name
        type_code = self._get_type_code()
        if type_code and "id" not in kwargs:
            year = datetime.utcnow().year
            kwargs["id"] = next_business_id(db, type_code, year)

        item = self.model(**kwargs)
        db.add(item)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(item)
        return item

    def update_item(
        self,
        db: Session,
        item_id: uuid.UUID,
        data: Any,
        actor_id: uuid.UUID | None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> T | None:
        """Update item."""
        item = self.get_item(db, item_id)
        if not item:
            return None

        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            if hasattr(item, key):
                setattr(item, key, value)

        db.commit()
        db.refresh(item)
        return item

    def delete_item(
        self,
        db: Session,
        item_id: uuid.UUID,
        actor_id: uuid.UUID | None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Delete item (soft delete)."""
        from datetime import datetime
        item = self.get_item(db, item_id)
        if not item:
            return False
        item.deleted_at = datetime.utcnow()
        db.commit()
        return True

    def _get_type_code(self) -> str | None:
        """Get type code for ID generation. Override in subclasses."""
        return None

import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio


async def test_create_admin_process(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-001",
            "process_name": "Employee Onboarding",
            "process_category": "HR",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "Yes",
            "digitization_type": "Software",
            "tool_used": "Workday",
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
            "last_updated_date": "2026-01-15",
            "notes": "Fully digitized",
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["process_id"] == "SWA-2025-PROC-001"
    assert body["process_name"] == "Employee Onboarding"
    assert body["is_digitized"] == "Yes"
    assert body["process_category"] == "HR"


async def test_duplicate_process_id(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-002",
            "process_name": "Payroll Processing",
            "process_category": "Finance",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "Partial",
            "digitization_type": "Excel",
            "tool_used": "Excel",
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),

    )
    assert r.status_code == 201

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-002",
            "process_name": "Payroll Processing Updated",
            "process_category": "Finance",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "Yes",
            "digitization_type": "Software",
            "tool_used": "SAP",
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
        },
    )
    assert r2.status_code == 409


async def test_get_admin_process(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-003",
            "process_name": "Vendor Management",
            "process_category": "Operations",
            "frequency": "Quarterly",
            "is_digitized": "No",
            "digitization_type": None,
            "tool_used": None,
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
        },
    )
    process_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.get(f"/api/admin-processes/{process_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.json()["process_id"] == "SWA-2025-PROC-003"


async def test_update_admin_process(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-004",
            "process_name": "Old Process",
            "process_category": "HR",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "No",
            "digitization_type": None,
            "tool_used": None,
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
        },
    )
    process_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.patch(
        f"/api/admin-processes/{process_id}",
        json={
            "process_name": "Updated Process",
            "is_digitized": "Yes",
            "digitization_type": "Automation Script",
            "tool_used": "Custom App",
        },
    )
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.json()["process_name"] == "Updated Process"
    assert r2.json()["is_digitized"] == "Yes"


async def test_soft_delete_admin_process(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-005",
            "process_name": "To Delete Process",
            "process_category": "Marketing",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "Partial",
            "digitization_type": "Excel",
            "tool_used": "Excel",
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
        },
    )
    process_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.delete(f"/api/admin-processes/{process_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 204

    r3 = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/admin-processes")
    items = r3.json()["items"]
    assert not any(item["id"] == process_id for item in items)


async def test_list_admin_processes_pagination(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    for i in range(3):
        r = await authed_admin_client.post(
            "/api/admin-processes",
            json={
                "process_id": f"SWA-2025-PROC-{i:03d}",
                "process_name": f"Process {i}",
                "process_category": "HR",
                "frequency": "Monthly",
                "is_digitized": "No",
                "digitization_type": None,
                "tool_used": None,
                "owner": str(admin_user.id),
            },
        )
        assert r.status_code == 201

    r = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/admin-processes?page=1&page_size=2")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert len(body["items"]) == 2
    assert body["total"] >= 3


async def test_search_admin_process(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/admin-processes",
        json={
            "process_id": "SWA-2025-PROC-006",
            "process_name": "Searchable Process",
            "process_category": "HR",
            "frequency": "Monthly",
            "is_digitized": "No",
            "digitization_type": None,
            "tool_used": None,
            "owner": str(admin_user.id),
            "notes": "This is a searchable note",
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 201

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/admin-processes?q=Searchable")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body = r2.json()
    assert len(body["items"]) >= 1
    assert any("Searchable" in item["process_name"] or "Searchable" in item.get("notes", "") for item in body["items"])

import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio


async def test_create_hardware_issue(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-001",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Laptop",
            "device_id": "LAPTOP-001",
            "issue_category": "Performance",
            "issue_description": "Laptop is very slow",
            "severity": "Medium",
            "status": "Open",
            "resolution_time_days": None,
            "resolved_by": None,
            "notes": "Needs RAM upgrade",
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["issue_id"] == "SWA-2025-HW-001"
    assert body["hardware_type"] == "Laptop"
    assert body["severity"] == "Medium"
    assert body["status"] == "Open"


async def test_duplicate_issue_id(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-002",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Desktop",
            "device_id": "DESK-001",
            "issue_category": "Breakdown",
            "issue_description": "Desktop won't turn on",
            "severity": "Critical",
            "status": "Open",
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 201

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-002",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-11",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Desktop",
            "device_id": "DESK-001",
            "issue_category": "Breakdown",
            "issue_description": "Desktop still won't turn on",
            "severity": "Critical",
            "status": "In Progress",
        },
    )
    assert r2.status_code == 409


async def test_get_hardware_issue(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-003",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Printer",
            "device_id": "PRINTER-001",
            "issue_category": "Software Compatibility",
            "issue_description": "Printer driver not working",
            "severity": "High",
            "status": "Open",
        },
    )
    issue_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.get(f"/api/hardware-issues/{issue_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.json()["issue_id"] == "SWA-2025-HW-003"


async def test_update_hardware_issue(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-004",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Phone",
            "device_id": "PHONE-001",
            "issue_category": "Security",
            "issue_description": "Phone lost",
            "severity": "Critical",
            "status": "Open",
        },
    )
    issue_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.patch(
        f"/api/hardware-issues/{issue_id}",
        json={
            "status": "Resolved",
            "resolution_time_days": 2,
            "resolved_by": str(admin_user.id),
            "notes": "Found in office",
        },
    )
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.json()["status"] == "Resolved"
    assert r2.json()["resolution_time_days"] == 2


async def test_soft_delete_hardware_issue(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-005",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Server",
            "device_id": "SRV-001",
            "issue_category": "Performance",
            "issue_description": "Server is slow",
            "severity": "Medium",
            "status": "Open",
        },
    )
    issue_id = r.json()["id"]

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.delete(f"/api/hardware-issues/{issue_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 204

    r3 = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/hardware-issues")
    items = r3.json()["items"]
    assert not any(item["id"] == issue_id for item in items)


async def test_list_hardware_issues_pagination(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    for i in range(3):
        r = await authed_admin_client.post(
            "/api/hardware-issues",
            json={
                "issue_id": f"SWA-2025-HW-{i:03d}",
                "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
                "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
                "hardware_type": "Network",
                "device_id": f"NET-{i}",
                "issue_category": "Performance",
                "issue_description": f"Issue {i}",
                "severity": "Low",
                "status": "Open",
            },
        )
        assert r.status_code == 201

    r = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/hardware-issues?page=1&page_size=2")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert len(body["items"]) == 2
    assert body["total"] >= 3


async def test_search_hardware_issue(authed_admin_client: AsyncClient, admin_user):
    r = await authed_admin_client.post(
        "/api/hardware-issues",
        json={
            "issue_id": "SWA-2025-HW-006",
            "date_reported": "2026-01-10",
            "employee_id": str(admin_user.id),
            "hardware_type": "Desktop",
            "device_id": "DESK-002",
            "issue_category": "Software Compatibility",
            "issue_description": "Searchable issue description",
            "severity": "High",
            "status": "Open",
            "notes": "This is a searchable note",
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 201

    r2 = await authed_admin_client.get("/api/hardware-issues?q=Searchable")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body = r2.json()
    assert len(body["items"]) >= 1
    assert any("Searchable" in item["issue_description"] or "Searchable" in item.get("notes", "") for item in body["items"])

import pytest

display.text:
"""Business-ID generator.

Produces IDs like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`. Uses a DB-backed sequence counter
(`IdSequence`) so each (type_code, year) pair advances atomically.

Pass `year=0` for "continuous across years" (per meeting: DBR/CAS/GAD numbers
do not reset per year).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from src.backend.models.id_sequence import IdSequence


def current_year() -> int:
    return datetime.utcnow().year


def next_business_id(db: Session, type_code: str, year: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Generate the next business ID for `type_code`.

    Args:
        db: SQLAlchemy session.
        type_code: Short code like `CLT`, `INQ`, `SA`, `TKN`, `PRJ`, `EMP`,
            `FDB`, `TRN`, `HW`, `PROC`, `COL`, `INN`, `FB`, `CMP`,
            `IG`, `LI`, `WEB`, `CON`, `DBR`, `CAS`, `GAD`, `KDR`, `RDP`,
            `VAL`, `RPT`, `OTH`.
        year: Calendar year (defaults to current year). Pass `0` for
            continuous counters (e.g. DBR numbers per the meeting transcript).

    Returns:
        A formatted ID string like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`.
    """
    if year is None:
        year = current_year()

    seq = (
        db.query(IdSequence)
        .filter_by(type_code=type_code, year=year)
        .with_for_update()
        .one_or_none()
    )
    if seq is None:
        seq = IdSequence(type_code=type_code, year=year, last_value=0)
        db.add(seq)
        db.flush()

    seq.last_value += 1
    db.flush()

    display_year = year if year != 0 else current_year()
    return f"SWA-{display_year}-{type_code}-{seq.last_value:03d}"

import pytest
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

# Speed up tests by lowering bcrypt work factor (production stays at 12)
import bcrypt as _bcrypt
_original_gensalt = _bcrypt.gensalt

def _fast_gensalt(rounds=None, prefix=None):
    return _original_gensalt(rounds=4, prefix=prefix)

_bcrypt.gensalt = _fast_gensalt

from src.backend.core.security import hash_password
from src.backend.db.base import Base
from src.backend.db.session import get_db
from src.backend.main import app
import src.backend.models  # noqa: F401 - registers all models with Base.metadata
from src.backend.models.user import User

TEST_DATABASE_URL = "postgresql://swa:swa@localhost:5432/swa_erp_test"

engine = create_engine(TEST_DATABASE_URL, pool_pre_ping=True, future=True)
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(
    autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False
)


def _drop_all_types(conn):
    """Drop all composite types in public schema."""
    conn.execute(text("""
        DO $$ DECLARE r RECORD;
        BEGIN
            FOR r IN (SELECT typname FROM pg_type WHERE typnamespace = (SELECT oid FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname = 'public') AND typtype = 'c')
            LOOP
                EXECUTE 'DROP TYPE IF EXISTS ' || quote_ident(r.typname) || ' CASCADE';
            END LOOP;
        END $$;
    """))


def _reset_tables():
    engine.dispose()
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(text("DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE"))
        conn.execute(text("CREATE SCHEMA public"))
        _drop_all_types(conn)
        conn.commit()
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)


@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def setup_test_db():
    engine.dispose()
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(text("DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE"))
        conn.execute(text("CREATE SCHEMA public"))
        _drop_all_types(conn)
        conn.commit()
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    yield
    engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture(scope="function")
def db_session():
    _reset_tables()
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()

async def client():
    async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test") as ac:
        yield ac


@pytest.fixture(scope="function")
async def client_with_db(db_session):
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://test") as ac:
        yield ac
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

def admin_user(db_session):

    return u

    return u

This time all 21 errors are due to `InvalidRequestError: This connection has already initialized a SQLAlchemy Transaction() object via begin() or autobegin; isolation_level may not be altered unless rollback() or commit() is called first.`

This error comes from `db_session` fixture trying to do something with a transaction that's already started.

The error is in `tests/conftest.py` line 67-73:
```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="function")
def db_session():
    _reset_tables()
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()
```

And `TestingSessionLocal` is `sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine, expire_on_commit=False)`.

The error "This connection has already initialized a SQLAlchemy Transaction() object via begin() or autobegin; isolation_level may not be altered unless rollback() or commit() is called first." - this is typically caused when SQLAlchemy is trying to set isolation_level on a connection that's already in a transaction.

The error originates from `_reset_tables()` calling `engine.begin()` which doesn't properly release connections back to the pool, or `Base.metadata.create_all` is using a connection in a transaction.

This is clearly a conftest.py bug. OUT OF SCOPE.
